argument-hint: '[<app>/<slug> | slug]'

<!-- Generated by `monoceros apply` from the agent-roles feature. Edits here
     are overwritten on the next apply. -->

Implement the plan the user named along with this skill.

## 1. Resolve the plan

Run `pwd` and list the plans on disk:

    find {{PLANS_DIR}} -name '*.md'

The app is the path segment right after `projects/` in the working directory.
`<app>/<slug>` is the unambiguous form; a bare slug resolves against the working
directory's app first, then against the whole list. A full path is used as it
stands. Exactly one match: use it. No match or several: show the list and ask
which one is meant, and touch nothing until they say.

No argument at all: show the plans for the working directory's app and ask.

Then read the plan's **Reply to the user in** field. Everything you say from
here on is in that language, from the first sentence, not English with a
translation after it. English when the field is missing.

## 2. Implement

Delegate to the `agent-roles-developer` subagent: the Agent tool in Claude
Code, the task tool in OpenCode, and in Copilot by asking for the
`agent-roles-developer` agent by name. It starts with an empty context, so name
the plan, the acceptance command and the language every time:

    Implement the plan at <the plan's absolute path>.
    Read the whole file first, including the out-of-scope and host-steps
    sections, then work the steps in order.
    Run <the acceptance command from the plan> and paste the tail of its real
    output.
    Reply in <the plan's language>.
    Report back. You do not delegate: the review is run from here.

**Gate on the deterministic check.** Before any review, the acceptance command
must have run green and the developer must have shown you the real output.
If it failed, hand the failure back to the same subagent (step 4 says how). Do
not fix the code yourself and do not weaken the criteria to make it pass.

## 3. Review

Then, the same way, the `agent-roles-reviewer` subagent:

    Review the change against the plan at <the plan's absolute path>.
    Establish the facts first: run the plan's acceptance command, read
    `git diff` and the untracked files from `git status` in full, and take the
    plan's steps and acceptance criteria out of it.
    Verdict on the very first line, evidence under it.
    Reply in <the plan's language>.

It is read-only by design, so it reports findings and never fixes them.

## 4. Repair, twice at most

On `CHANGES_REQUIRED`, hand the numbered items back to the **same** developer,
so it keeps its context and you send the findings, not the plan again: in
Claude Code with `SendMessage` to the id it ran under, in OpenCode with the
task tool and the same task id. Where your agent cannot continue a subagent,
start the developer again with the plan's path and the numbered findings. Then
gate on the acceptance command again, and review again.

Two repair rounds, and one earlier stop that matters more than the counter:
**if a finding survives a round, stop immediately.** Changing findings mean
progress; the same finding twice means the plan is wrong, and a third attempt
burns tokens to prove it.

When you stop without a PASS, say so as clearly as you would say PASS: what is
still open, what the reviewer said, and your read of why, which is usually the
plan itself.

## 5. Report

Whatever the outcome: the verdict, the acceptance output, what is running and
where to see it, the host steps the user still has to do, and the command to
carry on with. The user was away while this ran, and the report is all they
get.

Carry the developer's **Host steps** section over verbatim. It is the part that
gets dropped, and dropping it is why a run once ended with green tests, a
working app, and nothing reachable in the browser.
